Maine Space Corporation
Unleashing the Economic Potential of Maine's Space Industry
Testimony in Support of LD 1863 - An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Maine Space Corporation
Dawn M. DiBlasi, Esq., Chair Person Board Member, Maine Space Corporation
05/12/25 Before the Committee on Housing and Economic Development Committee
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and distinguished members of the Committee:
My name is Dawn M. DiBlasi, Esq. and I am the Chair of the Board of Directors of the Maine Space Corporation. I appreciate the opportunity to submit this testimony in support of LD 1863, a bill that will strengthen the Corporation's statutory foundation and ensure it can operate with the transparency, legal clarity, and governance expected of a public-purpose entity.
As the Chair and board member, I take seriously our responsibility to provide oversight and strategic direction to an organization that is stewarding an ambitious vision for Maine's future. The space economy is no longer science fiction--it is a growing sector generating jobs, innovation, and investment around the world. Maine has the talent, geography, and technical capacity to be a meaningful part of this opportunity. The Maine Space Corporation was created to make that vision actionable and coordinated--and LD 1863 is a necessary step toward that goal.
This legislation does three things that are especially important from a board governance perspective:
1. It clearly defines the Corporation as a quasi-independent state entity and an instrumentality of the State, which is critical for how we engage with federal and private sector partners. Without this clarity, we risk legal ambiguity that can limit our credibility or eligibility for external funding.
2. It aligns the Corporation with the requirements of a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, a step that not only unlocks federal funding but also reassures philanthropic and private donors that the Corporation operates in the public interest with the financial and operational standards of a nonprofit organization.
3. It modernizes board governance procedures to ensure smooth decision-making, continuity of operations, and protection of confidential business and technical information--protections essential to forming trusted partnerships with commercial collaborators.
LD 1863 is a forward-looking bill. It is about putting the right legal and organizational framework in place now, so that Maine can fully participate in and benefit from one of the most dynamic industries of the 21st century. I respectfully urge the Committee to support its passage.
Thank you for your time and your service to the people of Maine.

TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development Hearing Date: May 12, 2025
LD 1863 - "An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Maine Space Corporation"
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and members of the Housing and Economic Development Committee - good afternoon, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Neither For Nor Against LD 1863, "An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Maine Space Corporation."
This testimony is limited to the bill as it relates to taxation and Maine Revenue Services. The bill designates the Maine Space Corporation ("the Corporation") to be a nonprofit corporation and "clarifies" that the Corporation - when exercising the powers conferred to it by the Maine Space Corporation statute - is deemed to act as "an instrumentality of the State" and is a quasi-independent state entity that performs an essential governmental function. Further, the bill designates the Corporation as a nonprofit corporation under Maine law, whose duties, activities, and operations "must align with" the requirements under the Internal Revenue Code ("the Code"), Section 501(c)(3). The bill also specifies that certain information provided to, or developed by, the Corporation, including any financial statement, or supporting data of a financial statement, or tax return "of any person," is confidential.
1

While this testimony is neither for nor against LD 1863, the Administration is in support of clarifying the tax status of the Maine Space Corporation. The current law language regarding tax status is problematic and runs the risk of disagreement and dispute and is therefore detrimental to all concerned. This has been a concern of the Office of Tax Policy (OTP) since the creation of the Maine Space Corporation.
Although 5 MRSA �13201 provides that the Maine Space Corporation "is established as a body corporate and politic," the current statute does not provide that the Corporation is "an instrumentality of the State." Under current law, the Corporation is established as a body corporate and politic, with all the general powers of a corporation under 13-C M.R.S. � 302. The Maine Space Complex Fund "constitutes a continuing appropriation for the benefit" of the Corporation, and must be used, among other authorized expenditures, to "[p]ay all taxes owed by the corporation related to a corporation property or corporation project." Certain bonds issued by the Corporation are, together with interest on and income from the bonds, exempt from all taxes, including the Maine income tax. "Real and personal property, including funds" of the Corporation are exempt from levy and sale.
With respect to the proposed changes in LD 1863, it is relevant to note that Maine conforms to the federal income tax treatment of the Code, Section 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporations. Further, section 115(1) of the Code provides that gross income does not include income derived from the exercise of any essential governmental function and accruing to a state or any political subdivision thereof.
Although LD 1863 appears to helpfully address whether the Corporation shall be considered an instrumentality of the State for tax status purposes, further clean-up clarification is recommended - both in the bill and the underlying statute
2

- to make clear the apparent intended changes proposed by LD 1863. For example, the Committee may wish to consider the bill intention and language with respect to the bill's provision designating the Corporation as both an instrumentality of the State and a nonprofit corporation whose operations "must align with" the Code, Section 501(c)(3).
Separately, but of significance, the Administration notes that the bill's provisions on confidentiality as related to the tax or financial statement "of any person" should be clarified.
The preliminary estimated fiscal impact is not available at this time. The preliminary estimated administrative costs are nominal and can be absorbed within current budgetary allotments. The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill.

Testimony of Industry Representative in Support of LD 1863
Testimony in Support of LD 1863 - An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Maine Space Corporation Phillip Rench
Owner, Ossipee Hill Farm & Observatory Board Member, Maine Space Corporation
May 12, 2025 Before the Committee on Housing and Economic Development
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and distinguished members of the Committee:
My name is Phillip Rench, and I serve as Owner at Ossipee Hill Farm & Observatory. I am also a board member of the Maine Space Corporation. I appreciate the opportunity to submit this testimony in support of LD 1863.
As an industry representative, I strongly support the mission of the Maine Space Corporation to develop a coordinated space innovation ecosystem that strengthens Maine's economic and technological future. Industry needs partners who understand how to build the infrastructure, governance, and workforce necessary to support long-term growth. The Maine Space Corporation provides that leadership.
LD 1863 will give the Corporation the legal and structural clarity it needs to succeed. Codifying the Corporation as a quasi-independent state entity and instrumentality of the State ensures it can work credibly with both public and private partners. Aligning it with the requirements of a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization is equally essential--it allows the Corporation to compete for federal and philanthropic grants and to receive support from private capital.
For companies like mine, these legal provisions matter. They affect how we evaluate risk, how we collaborate, and how we invest in new technologies and partnerships. LD 1863 also ensures that our proprietary and technical information is protected--an important factor in any industry collaboration.
Maine is poised to become a leader in small satellite innovation, aerospace testing, and space data applications. With the Maine Space Complex, we have a unique opportunity to develop infrastructure that supports the full space technology lifecycle. But to do this, the Corporation must have the legal authority and nonprofit status to coordinate these activities and attract funding.
I respectfully urge the Committee to support LD 1863. This bill will help secure the foundation we

need to grow an industry that can bring high-paying jobs, private investment, and global visibility to Maine.
Thank you for your time and for your continued support of Maine's innovation economy.
